name: searchJiraIssuesUsingJql
description:
Search Jira issues using a JQL query; page with startAt or nextPageToken.

        Every matching issue comes back whole unless ``fields`` names the ones you
        want, which is the difference between a few hundred tokens a page and tens
        of thousands: pass e.g. ``["summary", "status", "assignee", "updated"]``
        and re-read the issues you actually need with ``getJiraIssue``.

jql.description: JQL query, e.g. project = PROJ AND status = 'In Progress' ORDER BY created DESC
jql.title: Jql

cloudId.description: cloudId of the Atlassian site, from getAccessibleAtlassianResources
cloudId.title: Cloudid

maxResults.title: Maxresults

startAt.description: 0-based index of the first result to return, for paging
startAt.title: Startat

nextPageToken.title: Nextpagetoken

name: getJiraIssueWorklogs
description:
List the worklogs on a Jira issue, with time spent, author and start date.

        The write side (``addWorklogToJiraIssue``) had no read counterpart, so an
        agent could log time over MCP but not read back what a site already had --
        which REST (``GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/worklog``) has always served.
